rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes threadIdx.x→threadIdx.z ONLY in the half-precision (float16) template specialization (line 23). The kernel is launched with block_size=256 as a 1D block, meaning threadIdx.z=0 for ALL threads. For half inputs, this would cause idx=blockIdx.x*256 for every thread, breaking the kernel. However, the input specification fixes dtype=torch.float32. Float32 dispatches to the generic template (line 13-18) which uses threadIdx.x (UNCHANGED). The mutated half-precision specialization is never executed with float32 inputs.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation exclusively affects the template specialization for half-precision (float16) data types at line 23. The AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF macro routes float32 tensors to the generic softsign_kernel template (lines 13-18), which retains the correct threadIdx.x indexing. Since the input specification locks dtype at torch.float32, the mutated half-precision code path is never invoked during testing. The mutation would cause catastrophic failure with float16 inputs (only every 256th element would be computed, rest would be garbage), but this requires changing the dtype configuration which is fixed per the contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: UNKILLABLE under current contract. The mutation only affects the float16/half template specialization, but the input dtype is fixed at float32. To kill this mutant would require changing dtype to torch.float16, which violates the fixed input specification contract. With float16, the mutant would produce drastically incorrect output since all 256 threads per block would write to the same index (threadIdx.z=0 always in 1D block launches).
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should treat dtype as a mutable configuration dimension, similar to shape/batch_size stress testing. For kernels with dtype-specialized code paths (like half-precision specializations), the test contract should either include multiple dtypes in the primary specification or explicitly document that dtype-specialized code is out of scope. This mutant exposes a coverage gap in dtype-sensitive kernels.
